newsitem.title: USA: Parker Drilling buys Mallard Bay for $338 million.
newsitem.headline: Parker Drilling buys Mallard Bay for $338 million.

text.p: Parker Drilling Co., a Tulsa, Okla.-based oil and gas drilling contractor, said Monday it signed a definitive agreement to buy Mallard Bay Drilling, a subsidiary of Houston-based Energy Ventures Inc., for $338 million.
Mallard Bay, based in New Iberia, La., owns 47 barge and platform rigs, that operate mostly in the shallow waters of the Gulf Coast. It also has operations in Nigeria, Peru and Argentina.
Currently, there are 162 rigs working in the Gulf of Mexico, according to Offshore Data Services drilling editor Tom Marsh.
"We've reached a point where, effectively, there are no rigs available," he said.
Parker specialises in drilling projects that are remote and also in the drilling of difficult, deep wells.

Parker said it would finance the acquisition by issuing debt. Parker stock was off 12.5 cents at $7 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading, while Energy Ventures was up $1.375 at $38.25.
